Documentation.description: Docs, examples, copy, and handbook/content updates.

Engineering Quality.description: Tests, refactors, CI, developer tooling, and maintainability.

Maintenance.description: Routine chores, dependency bumps, generated updates, and cleanup.

Platform.description: Data, infra, APIs, workers, migrations, and shared systems.

Product.description: User-visible capability, workflow, integration, or UI behavior.

Reliability.description: Bug fixes, performance, correctness, incidents, and hardening.

caveats: This uses public GitHub metadata, not private incidents, planning context, customer impact, or reviewer-only nuance.
PR body templates can be noisy, so scoring relies on visible non-comment text and caps any one signal.
Review impact is approximated from PR discussion because full review-thread collection for every PR would exceed the time box.

components.breadth: Distinct scopes and contribution categories touched.
components.collaboration: Review conversation and positive peer reactions on PRs.
components.depth: Average score of the engineer's five strongest PRs.
components.high_impact: Count of PRs in the top quartile of weighted PR impact for this dataset.
components.outcome_volume: Log-scaled sum of PR impact points so volume helps but cannot dominate alone.
components.quality: Testing evidence, issue linkage, and clear problem/change narratives.

method.definition: Impact is evidence that an engineer moved important product, reliability, or platform outcomes through reviewable work with validation and enough context for others to trust it.
method.exclusions: Obvious bot accounts and authors with fewer than 3 merged PRs in the window.

source: GitHub Search API /search/issues, one query per merged date
